subject.title: fix(google-meet): bound Calendar v3 events.list request deadline

question: Should Calendar v3 `events.list` lookups in the Google Meet plugin fail closed after a hardcoded 30s request deadline by default?
rationale: The implementation uses the existing guarded-fetch timeout path, but changing previously unbounded external API waits into default failures is upgrade-sensitive for slow Calendar workflows.

options.title: Accept 30s Default
options.body: After the test-helper repair, proceed with the branch because the cap matches the timeout campaign and bounds a real hang class without adding configuration.

options.title: Use Existing Timeout Source
options.body: Ask for Calendar helper defaults to inherit an existing Google Meet operation timeout where one is already available, while keeping a bounded fallback for direct helper use.

options.title: Pause For Policy
options.body: Keep the PR open until maintainers define a shared Google Meet timeout policy across Calendar, Meet, Drive, and OAuth calls.

recommendation.title: Accept 30s Default
recommendation.body: After the test-helper repair, proceed with the branch because the cap matches the timeout campaign and bounds a real hang class without adding configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Google Meet helper refactor history makes this the best available owner for the timeout contract choice.
